title: APN construction from two bent-component-free parts
summary: Construct a quadratic APN function with at least two source-defined bent-component-free subspaces by combining parts that individually have no bent component.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist a quadratic APN function $F$, not required to be biprojective, obtained by combining two parts that each have no bent Boolean component and satisfying $$\eta_m(\operatorname{NBF})\ge 2?$$ Construct such a function or infinite family, or prove that no such construction exists.

scope.domain: Quadratic APN functions and bent-component-free vectorial subspaces
assumptions: The ambient dimension is $n=2m$ as in the source definition of $\eta_m$
$F$ is quadratic and APN but need not be biprojective
The two constituent parts contain no bent component
scope.unresolved_remainder: A later theorem classifies the strict $(q,q)$-biprojective/subfield-property branch. Outside that branch, no inspected result constructs the required two-part APN function with $\eta_m(\operatorname{NBF})\ge2$ or proves nonexistence over the remaining general $(q,r)$ and non-biprojective domain.

citations.label: Gologlu, two bent-component-free parts problem
citations.locator: Problem III.5 and preceding paragraph, journal p. 4753

progress.summary: Problem III.5 and the preceding paragraph ask for the stated construction, explicitly allowing non-biprojective parts.
A later theorem exhausts the strict $(q,q)$-biprojective/subfield-property branch but leaves general $(q,r)$ and non-biprojective combinations unresolved.
